restatement: The card must produce two recovered, purely descriptive documents for the n8n template resolver repository at a pinned commit: a repository surface map (overview.md) and a module page for the template resolver (template-resolver.md). Every claim in them must carry a citation to the pinned source or an open question. A tool-run evidence check must report no findings (c1), and a fresh claim checker reading against the pinned commit must find no unsupported claim (c2). The documents must not propose changes (m1) and must not present an inference as a fact (m2).
brief_mismatch: The card goal and both criteria require two documents under docs/living/architecture/ to exist, but the card's Scope, files_scope and manifest (add/edit/remove) are all 'none'. The card also says 'change only the files listed in Scope'. Taken literally, the card forbids writing the very documents its goal requires. Consistent with that, the diff base..head is empty apart from 10 omitted docs/ephemeral paths. The reviewer brief's goal-critical question asks about 'frozen tests', but no criterion names a test file or trace.
verification_plan: Confirm the diff adds exactly the two recovered documents (overview and template-resolver module page) under the documented locations, and nothing outside card scope.
Confirm the manifest/files_scope authorizes those two paths; flag any write outside scope.
c1: find the evidence-check tool output (or a frozen test/gate trace for ar-01) and confirm it reports zero findings on both documents.

c2: sample claims from both documents and check that each carries a [src: path:line] citation or an [open: Qn] tag, and that the cited lines can plausibly support the claim as worded. Pay special attention to claims of absence ('no X exists', 'not tracked'), which a single file citation cannot prove.
c2: check that every [open: Qn] / [answer: Qn] tag resolves to a question that exists and that matches the claim.
m1: scan both documents for recommendations, 'should', 'fix', 'propose' or future-tense change language.

m2: scan for 'therefore', 'so', 'appears' and claims about runtime behavior. Check that inferences are either hedged or tagged open, not stated flatly. Also check that body text does not assert as fact what its own open question hedges.
Answer the goal-critical question: does each criterion hold when its frozen test is run? Identify the frozen test for c1 and c2, if any.

findings.title: Absence and 'not tracked' claims are cited to files that cannot support them

serves.scenario: A fresh claim checker reads '[src: .gitignore:1] [src: .gitignore:2]' as support for 'Neither node_modules/ nor dist/ is tracked'. It reads '[src: .gitignore:5]' as support for 'The pinned tree has no .github/ directory', and '[src: package.json:18-29]' as support for 'No CLI, server or script entry exists in the repository root'. A .gitignore entry does not prove a path is untracked or absent (files can be force-added), and a scripts block does not prove that no other entry file exists. Each of these is an unsupported claim, and each is an inference stated as fact (m2).

findings.rubric: ar-02: a fresh claim checker reads every claim against the pinned commit and finds no unsupported claim
findings.reproduction: At commit 712fcfd, open .gitignore lines 1-5 and package.json lines 18-29. Neither file says anything about which paths exist or are tracked, so the claims as worded go beyond what is cited. The smallest fix: cite a tree listing (e.g. git ls-tree at the pinned commit) or reword these as 'ignored by .gitignore' with the absence moved to an open question.
findings.location: docs/living/architecture/overview.md (Languages and manifests: .gitignore bullet; Build and test commands: node_modules/dist bullet; Entry points: last bullet)

findings.title: The module page's body asserts as fact the FOR-AS strict-mode failure that its own Q2 hedges as 'appears'

serves.scenario: The Execute path section states flatly that '${{item}} inside a loop adds item to the detected set' and that in strict mode it 'triggers the error in step 5 before resolution'. Q2 says this behavior only 'appears' to happen and was not checked. The body therefore states an inference as a fact.

findings.rubric: must not: state an inference as a fact
findings.reproduction: In template-resolver.md, compare the paragraph ending '[open: Q2]' under Execute path with Open question Q2. The body uses definite wording; Q2 uses 'appears to'. The smallest fix: hedge the body sentence to match Q2, or drop the hedge in Q2 if the source reading is conclusive.
